The initiative honors servicemen from the Civil War through World War I, including Buffalo Soldiers and a pioneering WWI aviator.
impact_innovation.extended_summary: At Concordia Cemetery in El Paso, some veterans' grave markers have crumbled, deteriorated, or vanished entirely. The Veterans Replacement Headstone Project is fixing that one stone at a time — and anyone can sponsor one for $155, which covers historical research, VA paperwork, and installation through a local monument company. The effort honors servicemen from the Civil War, Indian Wars (including Buffalo Soldiers), Spanish-American War, Mexican Revolution, and World War I. One recent restoration replaced the marker of 1st Lt. James "Buster" Biggs, a pioneering WWI Army aviator whose name now graces Biggs Army Airfield.

impact_innovation.title: Endangered, colorful garter snakes released into the wild for the first time
impact_innovation.summary: For the first time ever, 62 endangered San Francisco garter snakes born at the San Francisco Zoo were released into the wild in San Mateo County. The brilliantly colored reptiles have been on the endangered list since 1967, and only a few thousand remain — so this rewilding marks a real milestone for the species.
impact_innovation.extended_summary: The San Francisco garter snake is one of the most colorful reptiles in North America — and one of the rarest. It's been on the endangered species list since 1967, and after decades of drought, disease, invasive species, and poaching, only a few thousand remain. This fall, for the first time, 62 young snakes born at the San Francisco Zoo were released at sites across San Mateo County. Biologists call it a crucial step toward building self-sustaining populations, and it clears the way for more releases in the future.
